Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for agreeing to help with our security review. Attached is NebulaHQ's privacy intake questionnaire focusing on PII classification, access controls, and cross-border transfer concerns. We've also included a rough data flow diagram (nebulahq-dataflow-v1.png) that shows where our events hit Redwood and which fields we consider sensitive.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood processes any of our identifiers (email, phone, ssn fragments) in host-managed logs?
- Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for encryption-at-rest in us-west-2? If so, is the key material BYOK (customer holds full custody) or is it an envelope key managed by Redwood?
- Please provide your current subprocessors list and an estimate of where data is replicated (regions).
- We have a few specific DPA redlines; if you can share a point person for legal procurement that would be great.

Appreciate any artifacts you can share (KMS attestation, subprocessor CSV, data flow diagram mapping).

Best,
Olivia

Hi Olivia,

Thanks for the questionnaire and the diagram — helpful. Looping in Marcus (platform security) and Neha (privacy & compliance) to provide artifacts and answers. We'll produce a concise response and attach the artifacts you requested by EOD tomorrow.

Preliminary answers to move the conversation:
- Logs: by default we capture request metadata (request id, timestamp, route, tokenized prompts) but do not persist cleartext PII fields in platform logs. For customers that send identifiable fields in prompts, we recommend tokenization or client-side redaction.
- BYOK: we support customer-managed keys in hosted (us-west-2) as an opt-in feature. There are two modes:
  1) HSM-backed customer key where the customer controls key material via KMS and Redwood never has export capability (recommended).
  2) Envelope key managed by Redwood with a customer-owned root (suitable for managed PKI workflows).

We'll attach our KMS attestation and current subprocessor export for your legal team. If you can share your DPA redlines as a PDF, I'll route them to our contracts lead.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Hey Olivia — following up with the artifact pack. See attached: redwood-kms-attestation.pdf and redwood-subprocessors-2027-04.csv. Highlights below and inline answers to your numbered asks.

1) Host-managed logs and identifiers
- We do not intentionally index or search on PII fields in application logs. Operational traces include request_id, model, latency, and token counts.
- Customer-provided content (prompts/inputs) is stored transiently in our request store for X hours depending on the customer's retention policy; by default hosted accounts expire content after 30 days. Customers on Dedicated/Private can set retention to 0 for ephemeral workloads.

2) BYOK / KMS
- us-west-2: full BYOK supported (HSM-backed). When enabled, key material is customer-managed in their KMS tenant; Redwood only receives ciphertext and has no export capability.
- We also offer an envelope mode for managed customers who prefer Redwood to orchestrate rotation.

3) Subprocessors & replication
- CSV includes subprocessors for telemetry, observability, cloud infra (AWS, GCP), and analytics (third-party). Data residency: primary region us-west-2; secondary replication for high-availability is to us-east-1. Cross-border replication to eu-west-1 only occurs when a customer explicitly enables EU-region routing.

4) DPA and redlines
- Please send the redlines PDF; we'll have our contracts partner review and respond within 3 business days.

Attachments: redwood-kms-attestation.pdf (application/pdf, 210KB), redwood-subprocessors-2027-04.csv (text/csv, 6KB)

On the dataflow diagram: we've annotated common ingress points that would contain PII; happy to mark fields that can be tokenized or hashed before sending to Redwood.

—Marcus

Hi Olivia — consolidated answers below and next steps. Quoting your questions inline.

> Can you confirm whether any debug snapshots (heap/core dumps) that might be generated by transient errors could contain PII? If so, what's the retention and who has access?

Short answer: debug snapshots may contain in-memory content including PII if triggered during request processing. Access & retention:
- Snapshots are generated only under controlled incidents or explicit debug sessions; they are not created for standard inference traffic.
- Retention is 7 days by default and can be shortened; access is restricted to the SRE incident responders and platform debugging team (RBAC with Just-In-Time access logged in the audit trail).

> For BYOK HSM-backed keys: does Redwood support external attestation (e.g., customer-supplied HSM attestation or remote proof that keys were generated in an HSM)?

Yes — we support consumption of external attestation material and can accept customer-supplied attestation artifacts during onboarding. For ongoing audits, we can provide periodic attestation reports per contract (subject to an NDA/attestation-sharing agreement).

> Our legal team also asked whether Redwood will agree to add a clause that limits your subprocessors' ability to engage further subprocessors without prior notice to NebulaHQ (we can propose wording).

We are open to reasonable contractual language that requires notice for subcontracting changes and to provide a right to object within a defined window. I'll loop in contracts@redwood.com to triage your redline.

Next steps:
- Contracts (contracts@redwood.com) — please review redlines-dpa-nebulahq.pdf and propose availability for a 30-minute sync.
- Marcus/Neha: we'll mark the dataflow diagram with recommended fields to tokenise and return an annotated PNG to Olivia by EOD Thursday.
- Olivia: please confirm if NebulaHQ requires retention shorter than our 30-day default for hosted content; we can propose a custom retention SOW.
